findings.title: `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` builds its expected occurrence with the wrong group key
findings.description:
The expected occurrence is built with group key `"val1"`, but the handler is evaluated with group key `"group_key"`, so the first assertion at lines 546-560 should fail.

- **Expected side:** `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)` gives a fingerprint of `["<id>:val1"]` (via `build_fingerprint`, `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:172-176`).
- **Actual side:** `evaluate_group_key_value("group_key", ...)` calls `build_occurrence_and_event_data("group_key", ...)` at `detector.py:299-301`, giving `["<id>:group_key"]`.
- **Why they can't compare equal:** `IssueOccurrence` is a plain `@dataclass(frozen=True)` (`src/sentry/issues/issue_occurrence.py:66-67`) with field-wise equality. Only `StatusChangeMessage.__eq__` is patched in `setUp`.

Fix: pass `"group_key"` to `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` on line 537.

findings.title: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` is now an uninstantiable abstract class registered on a production group type
findings.description:
The handler now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with a body of `pass`, leaving four abstract members unimplemented: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (`processors/detector.py:142-170`).

- **Effect:** `Detector.detector_handler` runs `group_type.detector_handler(self)` (`src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86`), which raises `TypeError` for any detector of type `metric_alert_fire`. Before this change the handler instantiated and returned `[]`.
- **Blast radius:** `process_detectors` has no guard around handler construction (`detector.py:52-58`), so one such detector aborts the whole batch.
- **Why not FAIL:** `process_detectors` has no callers under `src/` yet, so this is latent.

Either add stub implementations or leave `detector_handler` unset on `MetricAlertFire` until the handler is real. The TODO on line 10 ("This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction") is also stale now.

findings.title: Expected occurrences are built with values that do not match the evaluated input
findings.description:
Several tests build the expected occurrence with `value=6` while evaluating a different value:

- `test_state_results_multi_group`: `group_2` is evaluated with 10 (line 177).
- `test_results_on_change`: evaluated with 100 (lines 488-491).
- `TestEvaluate.test_dedupe`: evaluated with 8 (lines 508-511).

These pass only because the mock ignores `value`. As a result, no test verifies that `evaluate_group_key_value` forwards the right `value` to the new hook. Have the mock record `value` (for example in `evidence_data`) and pass the real values.

findings.title: No `process_detectors` test covers the resolve path
findings.description:
The new `process_detectors` tests only assert `PayloadType.OCCURRENCE` production. Nothing exercises the path where a stateful detector goes back to OK and `create_issue_occurrence_from_result` (`detector.py:73-87`) sends a `StatusChangeMessage` as `PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE`.

Separately, `test_state_results_multi_group` uses `assert_has_calls(..., any_order=True)` without checking `call_count == 2`, so extra produces would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Docstrings drift from the new return type and the new hook is undocumented
findings.description:
- `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` still says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`"; it now returns a dict keyed by group key.
- `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (lines 166-170) is the only abstract member of the class without a docstring. It should state what `value` and `new_status` mean, and that it is only called for non-OK statuses.

findings.title: Duplicate-key guard removed with no check that dict key matches `result.group_key`
findings.description:
Returning a dict makes duplicate group keys structurally impossible, so dropping the logged-error branch is reasonable. `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` keeps key and `result.group_key` in sync at line 243. A custom `DetectorHandler.evaluate` could still return mismatched keys, and nothing would notice.

Related: `get_group_key_values` is annotated `dict[str, int]` (line 159), but a `None` key is used in `test_state_results` (test file line 148). The annotation should be `dict[DetectorGroupKey, int]`.

findings.title: Minor test-scaffolding leftovers
findings.description:
- `TestProcessDetectors.setUp` only calls `super().setUp()` and can be deleted.
- `build_handler(detector_type=...)` (lines 101-106) has no caller passing that argument.
- `create_detector_and_conditions(type=...)` shadows the builtin and hardcodes `"handler_with_state"` instead of using `self.handler_state_type.slug`.

findings.title: `PriorityLevel(new_status)` conversion is safe
findings.description: `DetectorPriorityLevel` is `OK=0` plus `LOW`/`MEDIUM`/`HIGH` aliased to the `PriorityLevel` values (`src/sentry/workflow_engine/types.py:8-12`). The conversion only runs in the `else` branch after `OK` is excluded, so it cannot raise `ValueError`.

findings.title: `Detector.group_type` extraction is correct
findings.description: `builtins.type[GroupType]` is the right annotation, since the model's `type` field shadows the builtin in class scope. `detector_handler` reuses the property with unchanged behaviour and logging, and the return type matches `GroupTypeRegistry.get_by_slug` (`src/sentry/issues/grouptype.py:104-107`).

structured_findings.summary: `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` builds its expected occurrence with the wrong group key
`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` is now an uninstantiable abstract class registered on a production group type
Expected occurrences are built with values that do not match the evaluated input
No `process_detectors` test covers the resolve path
Docstrings drift from the new return type and the new hook is undocumented
Duplicate-key guard removed with no check that dict key matches `result.group_key`
